claims.statement: EU energy-efficiency guidance emphasizes measurement, monitoring, control, quality, and independent verification of energy savings, including metered savings and statistically representative checks.
EU guidance defines energy performance contracting around verified and monitored savings and notes that quality labels, measurement methodologies, and certified providers can support uptake.
Hypothesis: a low-cost standardized certificate for smaller multi-family projects can serve a segment below traditional ESCO economics and create lender or installer willingness to pay.

contrary_evidence: Certified energy auditors and ESCOs already perform measurement and verification for larger projects.
EU guidance notes that traditional energy-performance contracts often need large contract values, which may leave small buildings uneconomic even with cheaper software.

economics.acquisition_route: Hypothesis: start as the measurement subcontractor for three auditors/installers, then obtain lender recognition for repeat portfolio use.
economics.founder_net_worth_path: Hypothesis: 50 buildings in year 2, 500 in year 4, and 2000 annual building cycles across Poland and neighbors in year 7 at 6000 PLN average revenue yields 12M PLN annual revenue. At 15-22% operating margin, a 2-4x revenue value, and 55-70% ownership, founder equity could exceed 5M PLN after lender-channel repeatability.
economics.founder_time: Hypothesis: 12-18 hours/week for modeling and partner delivery; site inspection remains with qualified auditors.
economics.gross_margin_basis: Hypothesis: 55-70% early with expert baseline review, rising to 75-82% as ingestion and exception handling automate.
economics.payback: Hypothesis: 5-10 months at 5000-12000 PLN channel acquisition cost and 15000-30000 PLN annual revenue per active partner.
economics.pricing: Hypothesis: 3000-8000 PLN per building measurement cycle plus 300-800 PLN/month monitoring for larger portfolios.
economics.retention_or_repeat: Hypothesis: each building produces baseline and follow-up events; partner retention depends on a continuing retrofit pipeline and accepted certificates.

fingerprint.compounding_advantage: Predicted-versus-realized savings corpus by building archetype, intervention, contractor, climate, and operating pattern
fingerprint.customer: Polish condominium boards and the installers, auditors, ESCOs, or lenders serving 10-100-unit buildings
fingerprint.distribution_mechanism: Energy auditors, retrofit installers, banks, subsidy advisors, and property-management software
fingerprint.offer_and_business_model: Standardized baseline, data-quality check, weather-normalized realized-savings report, and shareable outcome credential
fingerprint.payer_and_paid_event: Installer, ESCO, lender, or condo board pays at baseline approval and again when the realized-savings certificate is issued
fingerprint.problem_trigger: Retrofit proposal, financing decision, contractor guarantee, or first 12-month post-retrofit review

founder_fit: Strong fit with causal modeling, weather normalization, and quantitative evaluation.
Parents' renewable-energy network can identify installer and auditor workflows while avoiding direct access to private data without consent.
Can start with retrospective, permissioned bill datasets and desktop analysis.
Product creates reusable outcome benchmarks and can later support underwriting.
risks: Bad baselines can unfairly reward or penalize contractors; model assumptions must be transparent and independently reviewable.
Meter and household data permission complexity.
Long outcome windows delay proof and cash conversion.

structure.control_point: accepted weather-normalized baseline and realized-savings certificate
structure.critical_dependency: permissioned longitudinal meter data and recognition by retrofit finance channels

thesis: A weather- and occupancy-aware measurement service for Polish condominium boards that compares predicted and realized savings after heating, insulation, or control-system retrofits. The paid certificate helps installers, ESCOs, and lenders evidence outcomes, while each building adds to a local archetype benchmark for future underwriting and guarantees.
title: Retrofit Reality: Verified Savings Benchmark for Condo Boards
uncertainties: Condo-board decision cycles and access to complete pre/post energy bills may be slow.
A certificate's value depends on lender, insurer, subsidy, or installer recognition.
The 60000 PLN capital estimate and all numeric commercial assumptions below are planning hypotheses.
